structure.note: 537,582,089 listed 'A' shares (par CHF 1.00) and 537,582,089 unlisted 'B' shares (par CHF 0.10). Each share has one vote, and each share's portion of net profit and liquidation proceeds is in proportion to its par value. All 'B' shares are held by Compagnie Financière Rupert, which also holds 6,418,850 'A' shares: 10.18% of the capital and some 51% of the voting rights. The directors regard Compagnie Financière Rupert as the Group's controlling party. The report states there were no other shareholders holding at least 3% of the voting rights at 31 March 2025.

notes: Fiscal year ended 31 March 2025 (FY2025, matching data.js 'Mar 2025'); all figures from the Richemont Annual Report and Accounts 2025 on richemont.com. Reported in EUR, converted exactly from € millions. OWNERSHIP: Johann Rupert holds his interest through Compagnie Financière Rupert (CFR), of which he is the sole General Managing Partner; Anton Rupert, a non-executive director, is also a partner. The report does not say how CFR's own equity is split among its partners, so the stake is recorded in family (labelled as CFR) and leader.pctEconomic is null. Johann Rupert does not appear in the directors' table of individual 'A' share holdings. The 10.18% is CFR's share of the Company's capital (par value), which is also the basis for profit and liquidation entitlements; the compensation report and note 37 round it to '10% of the equity'. Voting control is 'some 51%' (note 39: 51%). 'Parties associated with Mr Johann Rupert and Compagnie Financière Rupert held a further 2 921 335 'A' shares' (0.3% of voting rights); their % of capital is not stated, so it is not added. relation 'founder': his board biography states 'He founded Richemont in 1988'. No other holder of 3% or more of votes, so largestHolders is empty. BUYBACKS: 0 under the site's rule that purchases covering employee plans are not cash returned to shareholders (same rule as the Tencent pilot and the UBS and Fortescue records). The cash-flow statement shows 'Acquisition of treasury shares' of €104m (0.7 million shares), which note 30.2 says hedges obligations under share-based compensation plans; proceeds from treasury share sales on option exercises were €162m, so the net flow was an inflow. There was no buyback programme for cancellation. To count the gross purchases instead, use 0.10. DIVIDENDS: CHF 2.750 per 'A' share and CHF 0.275 per 'B' share paid in September 2024; €1,710m to owners of the parent; nothing to non-controlling interests in FY2025. STOCK COMP: €118m equity-settled share-based compensation expense, including €1m in discontinued operations (YNAP). GEOGRAPHY: the four main areas; the note also gives country detail (e.g. United States €4,498m, mainland China €2,931m, Japan €2,186m).
